title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: single-trail distinguished-point rho in GT

claims.statement: For a uniform nonidentity P in BLS12-381 G1 and an independent uniform z in GT, the attack in proof.md returns Q=[a]Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z under the pinned pairing convention, using at most 2^127.85 total target-group-operation equivalents (dense Fp12 multiplications, C=20,000). It computes g=e(P,Q0) (a generator) and solves z=g^a by a SINGLE-TRAIL distinguished-point Pollard rho on GT: one continuous trajectory F^i(X_0), F(X)=X*M_{H(X)} with R=2^20 adding entries, costs ONE dense Fp12 multiplication per step (no tortoise/hare factor). It stores each distinguished point keyed by the EXACT full reduced tower representation of the element (no fingerprint, hence no false matches) with its (A,B); the trajectory detects its own self-collision when a stored exact key repeats (it has re-entered its cycle), giving a=(A_j-A_i)/(B_i-B_j) mod r. The partition index H=bits 0..19 and the DP predicate (bits 20..83 zero) read w = the two least-significant 64-bit limbs of the first reduced tower coefficient the reference multiplication outputs (all 64 bits present; no Montgomery/flat export in the walk). The distinguished density is ~2^-64 and the routing bits are balanced by the equidistribution of the first tower coefficient bits over GT; this is SUPPORTED by the experiment, which computes real BLS12-381 GT elements (random Fp12 ^ cofactor, verified by g^r=1) and finds the DP-predicate slice (bits 20..31) and routing slice (bits 84..95) statistically uniform (chi^2/dof ~0.98 and ~1.02) with the measured density matching 2^-12, extrapolating to the 64-bit predicate by the same mechanism (the one modelling assumption beyond the random-mapping collision-time model). Table exponents are drawn from the rules' fresh uniform algorithm coins (512 bits reduced mod r, bias<2^-256). DP reports are routed to 2^16 separate storage nodes, each an independent machine addressing <2^64 bytes with a hard per-node cap of 2^49 records <=2^10 bytes each = <=2^59 bytes/node, and a hard global cap N_cap=2^65 reports (~2.3x the ~2^63.8 mean; Chernoff-negligible overflow-to-failure); routing and report work (2^17 instr/report) and node set-up (2^20 instr/node) are charged and negligible, and no >2^64-byte address space is assumed. The hard budget is T_total=ceil(1.3*k0)+L_cap (k0=sqrt(2*r*ln(1/0.61)), L_cap=20/theta); a single trajectory has rho<=T with probability 1-0.61^1.69=0.566 and is then detected within T_total unless its cycle is DP-free (short-cycle bound <=2^-28.7), the re-entry-to-DP gap exceeds L_cap (<=2^-28.9) or the repeat is unusable (<=1/r), giving a supported success lower bound >=0.566-2^-27.8>=0.39 (no transfer margin; the same clean P(rho<=T) bound as my accepted Floyd submission whose walk is identical). The analysis is single-processor (serial; score is processor-count independent). Each multiplication is <=1.014 units; W=(1.3*k0+L_cap)*1.014=2^127.819 plus negligible report/one-time work, rounded to 2^127.85. Peak memory <=2^76 bytes total (DP records <=2^75 plus the adding table), <=2^59 bytes/node (reported only; access charged). Preprocessing <=2^31 units included; nonuniform advice 0 bytes. Classical cold attack, no uncharged advice or quantum steps; generic square-root accounting, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: On REAL BLS12-381 GT elements (formed as a random Fp12 element raised to the cofactor (p^12-1)/r in a self-contained blst Fp2/Fp6/Fp12 tower, each verified by g^r=1), histogram the exact coefficient-bit slices the single-trail DP rho reads: the distinguished-point slice (bits dp_shift..) and the routing slice (bits route_shift..). Report chi^2/dof against the uniform null for each slice and the distinguished-point count at the measured density. chi^2/dof ~1 and a matching density support the ~2^-64 DP density and balanced routing over the structured subgroup GT. Production-form evidence for the one heuristic beyond the random-mapping collision-time model.
